
Strategy: Stronger-signal merge. The window bonus for 28-48 is the larger of one third of the item and the triangular peak of 20 at 38, so large items use scaling, small items the peak. The penalty for 6-22 is likewise the larger of half the item and the triangular peak of 20 at 15. Near-exact of 6 or less earn 25. Ranking changes when item size flips which term is larger. It may fail if the larger term overvalues the bands.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (max(item / 3, 20 - abs((r - item) - 38) // 2) if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (max(item / 2, 20 - abs((r - item) - 15) // 2) if 6 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) + (25 if r - item <= 6 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the floating window with roundness: fits win by default, residuals from 25 to 45 above the smallest residual gain 20, residuals in [8,22] lose 15, and every residual gains 10 minus its distance to the nearest multiple of 10. The ranking changes when a residual enters the floating window or nears a multiple of 10. It may help by combining a floating sweet spot with clean splits; it may fail if roundness is noise.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    s = min([r - item for r in bins])
    return [-(r - item) + (20 if (r - item) >= s + 25 and (r - item) <= s + 45 else 0) - (15 if (r - item) >= 8 and (r - item) <= 22 else 0) + (10 - min((r - item) % 10, 10 - (r - item) % 10)) for r in bins]
```

A 10 bonus covers 30-45 when item size is 1 modulo 3 for all items. The penalty for 6-22 is half the item for large items and a flat 20 for small ones. Ranking changes when item size flips the split. It may fail if the size split misroutes items.

